title: How would you estimate how many hotel rooms there are in Paris?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many hotel rooms are there in Paris?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A harder one: you work backwards from guest nights to rooms, dividing by occupancy and guests per room. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many hotel rooms are there in Paris?

The approach

Guest nights per year ÷ 365 ÷ share of rooms filled ÷ guests per room.

Tip: Keep your page tidy: one line per step, the running total circled at the end.

Step by step

  1. Hotel guest nights in Paris per year: 50M
  2. ÷ 365 days in a year
  3. ÷ 75% rooms filled on an average night
  4. ÷ 1.6 guests per room

That gives about 114k rooms.

Does it make sense?

Around 115,000 rooms. Short-term rentals take some visitors who would otherwise stay in hotels.

Why occupancy belongs in the denominator

The original approach converts guest nights into occupied room nights using the average 1.6 guests per room, then scales up for rooms that are empty. At 50 million guest nights, 1.6 guests per room means 31.25 million occupied room nights. Dividing by 365 and 75% occupancy gives about 114,000 available rooms.

If average occupancy were 85% rather than 75%, the same guest demand would require about 101,000 rooms. A higher occupancy assumption means fewer rooms are needed to house the same guests, not more. This reversal is a useful sanity check.

Ask whether "Paris" means the city proper or the broader metropolitan area. Hotels and short-term rentals should not be mixed without adjusting the scope. A tourism case may also require a separate estimate of leisure versus business guests and average nightly room price.
